notes: S130-01. The opening says that the vertical arrows are morphisms of extensions by twisted copies of Z^{d_0}, more specifically by T_{d_0} and its inverse image. The upper margin qualifies this by vanishing of the second homotopy objects of two indicated bases. This records the manuscript assertion; the first reader did not attempt a homotopy-exact-sequence proof. Root’s later conditional check is recorded in N130-16. Historical status: the phrase 'vertical arrows' above records the pre-blind noun reading and is superseded by root audit B02. The current transcription is les \unsure{fibres|flèches} verticales sont des morphismes; fibres is the leading visual reading and flèches remains an alternative. The mathematical check retains its separately stated conditional scope.

S130-02. Formula (210) identifies a local system by inverse image and by the first homotopy or homology of fibres, then defines a starred restriction. The following paragraph asserts an extension by that restriction and repeats a vanishing qualification in the margin. These claims are carried as background, not certified by a transcription check.

S130-03. The lower brace (211) introduces coproduct families G, P, T and their starred restrictions. Its intended group/torsor terminology is recorded, but the B-leading right summand is not silently replaced by the mathematically expected G.

S130-04. Single horizontal index strokes were compared occurrence by occurrence. Comma-dash-comma occurs in the opening D, the first T and source D of (210), its final restricted D, both extension Π indices, the cancelled coproduct's right Π, the live summation tuple, and the P/T summands. The two restriction-row T indices and fibre P/D indices have no separate commas. The extension-par T*, second margin D*, and right B/G summand have one comma before the dash. The upper margin's middle index remains doubtful. Historical status: the classification of the live summation tuple as one continuous stroke above is superseded by root audit B18/B26. The current tuple is (d_0,\mathord{-\, -},d_r)\in\mathbb N^{r+1}, with two distinct continuation strokes between its commas. The other occurrence-specific index descriptions remain applicable.

S130-05. The second-homotopy signs in both qualifications and the first-homotopy signs in the two local-system descriptions have Π-like graphic forms. All four use a capital-leading local doubt; the homotopy meaning does not by itself establish lowercase pi. The unambiguous groupoid Π symbols in the extension paragraph retain capitals and the visible tilde.

S130-06. The (210) connector is reproduced as a shaft with its short terminal downward return. The cap and lower spur do not establish a full two-sided head. No direction or morphism property was inferred from mathematical need.

S130-07. The first annotation consists of syst. loc., a separate question-mark-like raised curl, and the added parenthesized local-isomorphism formula. The leaders associate these with T_d0; the latter is physically above the sur phrase. H's de rang d_0 has no separate matching ink, and loc. is not expanded in the transcription. Historical status: the combined attachment description above is superseded by root audit B07/B25. The current transcription attaches the syst. loc. caption and its separate doubtful curl by two curved arms beside T_{d_0}. The parenthesized local-isomorphism formula is a separate raised annotation over the opening sur phrase, with its own long line beneath it. The two attachments are drawn separately.

S130-08. Three cancelled passages were checked independently: the initial T* fragment inside (210), the whole coproduct before (211), and the short condition under the first live coproduct. Their full surviving baselines are preserved in both the proposal and second boxes. Crossing strokes do not justify extracting an earlier B from the left G/B or a definite earlier numeral from the label 210.

S130-09. The right summand of the first (211) row has two right bowls, so B leads G; the left letter remains G-leading because its broad left curve and retracing differ. These are visual/notation consistency checks, not a proof or a mathematical correction.

S130-10. The last live summation condition contains a point followed by a short dash after d_1, represented literally. No additional inequality after d_1 is supplied. N and both occurrences of Z have visible doubled oblique strokes.

S130-11. In the local-system description the reduced ou and the two later paired marks have very similar minimal shapes. The later marks are drawn literally and their ou/separator interpretation remains open. There are no separately written choix letters. The low commas after the first homotopy symbol, H_1, and P_Δr remain.

S130-12. The compressed final word is ranked dire, dira, dés from its visible joins; the following baseline begins les restrictions à. The entire starred passage lies within the continuing large brace. No final full stop is added after D*_Δr.

S130-13. The manuscript page number is 64 and the pencil archive number is 129. The first display label remains unsure210 because its middle digit has a tall upright and a low retraced loop; a separate earlier numeral is not established. The lower label 211 is clear. Numbering sequence was not used to force the crowded digit. Historical status: unsure210 above is the pre-blind rendering and is superseded by root audit B12/B25. The current tag is 2\unsure{1|6|0}0: the outer 2 and 0 are clear, while the middle digit retains 1 first with 6 and 0 as alternatives. No separate earlier numeral is reconstructed.

S130-14. Every supplied C uncertainty, including the unindexed nested uncertainties, and every C deletion/insertion was checked against this page’s images. The first reader used 24 crops. Root subsequently made and inspected one first crop of the previously uncropped H-only initial illegibility mark, confirming that no separate main-baseline word precedes les. Its already-planned blind box is B02; no duplicate box was added. Before the blind baseline was fixed, root added B25 and B26 for the complete multiline displays210 and211, supplementing their individual line/detail boxes.

S130-15. The line count is 32 physical reading baselines, including the manuscript and archive numbers, the margin lines, the annotation line, and the three summation-condition baselines. Subscripts and raised loc are not counted as independent baselines. The reconciliation list fixes the units explicitly.

MC130-R: for a locally trivial bundle with connected fibre (C*)^d, the homotopy exact sequence identifies the kernel of π₁(E)→π₁(B) with Z^d modulo the image of π₂(B). Thus π₂(B)=0 suffices for the fibre lattice to inject and to equal that kernel. Root checked this consequence using the standard exact sequence as background, and the coordinate retraction of (C*)^d onto (S¹)^d. This does not prove that every written object satisfies the bundle hypotheses or settle Π/π glyph case. See review/mathematical_checks.md, MC130-R.

Blind audit: all23 differing boxes were inspected. Seven boxes changed: the opening noun now leads with fibres while retaining flèches; pose/posera and de/du remain explicit; the first number has only its middle digit uncertain (1/6/0); the two annotations retain separate leaders and placement; and the live tuple in (211) has two strokes. Both whole-display boxes record the corresponding changes. The margins, capped connectors, cancellations, B/G distinction, Pi case alternatives, final dire/dira/dés, and foliation129 remain as visually adjudicated.
